Case_17008/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of endometrial biopsy (40x)

description.short_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of endometrial biopsy showing granuloma formation (40x).
description.detailed_description: This hematoxylin and eosin-stained section of an endometrial biopsy shows a granuloma characterized by a central area of necrosis surrounded by epithelioid histiocytes and a rim of lymphocytes. The surrounding tissue displays inflammatory infiltrates. The magnification is approximately 40x, highlighting cellular details.

description.short_caption: Gram stain of endometrial biopsy showing bacterial colonies.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of an endometrial biopsy at 40x magnification. The central area contains dense, purple-stained bacterial colonies, indicative of Gram-positive organisms. Surrounding the colonies is a background of lighter-stained tissue, likely representing the endometrial stroma. The distribution and density of the bacteria suggest localized infection.

Case_17008/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Methenamine silver stain of endometrial biopsy (40x)

description.short_caption: Methenamine silver stain of endometrial biopsy showing fungal elements (40x magnification).
description.detailed_description: This is a high-magnification (40x) methenamine silver stain of an endometrial biopsy. The image highlights fungal elements, which appear as darkly stained, branching, septate hyphae against a green background. The surrounding tissue is less prominently stained, providing contrast to the fungal structures. The methenamine silver stain is commonly used to identify fungal organisms in tissue samples.
